headlines.title: Why Verizon Communications (VZ) Is Getting Attention Today
headlines.summary: Verizon Communications (VZ) has stepped into the debt market spotlight after setting detailed pricing terms for five separate cash tender offers, targeting up to US$500 million of its outstanding notes across multiple maturities. Against this tender offer backdrop, Verizon Communications shares trade at US$46.12 after a small 1 day dip, yet the 7 day share price return of 5.63% and year to date gain of 13.

headlines.title: Bigleaf Networks Named to The Fast Mode’s Vendors to Watch 2027 List for Innovation in Broadband Connectivity
headlines.summary: TIGARD, Ore., November 05, 2026--Bigleaf Networks, a leading provider of intelligent network optimization solutions, today announced its inclusion in The Fast Mode Vendors to Watch 2027, recognizing technology providers positioned to advance connectivity and digital infrastructure in the coming year.

headlines.title: A 71-Year-Old Gets $1200 A Month In Dividends From SCHD.  He Could Double His Investment Income By Swapping SCHD For Verizon. There’s Just One Problem
headlines.summary: Swapping one dividend holding for another could more than double a retiree's monthly checks. But a single bad board decision could erase that gain and chip away at his savings when he has the least time to recover.

headlines.title: 5 High-Yield Dividend Stocks Paying Up to 6% With Payouts Built to Last
headlines.summary: A fat yield means nothing if the check bounces. Five payers across telecom, tobacco, pharma, real estate and pipelines show how to test coverage, and one of them carries a debt pile that could threaten its raise streak.

headlines.title: Can Verizon's 5G Expansion in the 2026 NFL Season Drive Future Growth?
headlines.summary: VZ is expanding its NFL partnership with advanced 5G and private wireless technology to enhance stadium operations, official communications and fan connectivity in 2026.

description: Verizon Communications Inc., through its subsidiaries, engages in the provision of communications, technology, information, and streaming products and services to consumers, businesses, and governmental entities worldwide. It operates in two segments, Verizon Consumer Group (Consumer) and Verizon Business Group (Business). The Consumer segment provides wireless services across the wireless networks in the United States under the Verizon and TracFone brands and through wholesale and other arrangements; and fixed wireless access (FWA) broadband through its wireless networks, as well as related equipment and devices, such as smartphones, tablets, smartwatches, and other wireless-enabled connected devices. The segment also offers wireline services in the Mid-Atlantic and Northeastern United States, as well as Washington D.C. through its fiber-optic network, Verizon Fios product portfolio, and a copper-based network. The Business segment provides wireless and wireline communications services and products, including FWA and wireline broadband, advanced communication services, corporate networking, security and managed network, local and long-distance voice, and network access services to deliver various IoT services and products to businesses, government customers, and wireless and wireline carriers in the United States and internationally. The company distributes its products and services through direct channels, company-operated stores, digital and omnichannel platforms, indirect agents, business solution resellers, and national retailers. The company was formerly known as Bell Atlantic Corporation and changed its name to Verizon Communications Inc. in June 2000. Verizon Communications Inc. was incorporated in 1983 and is headquartered in New York, New York.
